question: Ongoing instability in Iran and rising geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have brought about a sharp increase in the cost of electricity and gas, as well as fuels such as petrol and diesel. This has had a direct effect on household energy bills and on European companies’ operating costs.
These dynamics are placing a significant burden on citizens’ purchasing power and on the competitiveness of the European production system, particularly in the most energy-intensive sectors.

The persistent increase in energy costs also risks having an inflationary effect on the economy as a whole, affecting the prices of goods and services and creating further difficulties for households, workers and economic activities, which have already been hit by the recent international crises. In this context, it seems necessary to consider extraordinary intervention instruments at European level.
In the light of the above, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Does it intend to consider setting up an extraordinary European fund to support Member States in containing the impact of price rises on households and businesses?
Does it envisage adopting specific Europe-wide measures to set a price ceiling for fuels and energy supplies, in order to soften the effects of the current geopolitical tensions on European citizens?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) Europe is facing a serious situation when it comes to fossil fuels, which threatens to impose further costs on households and business. A united, coordinated European response is needed in order to avoid fragmented national approaches and disruptive signals to the market: solidarity, transparency, and cooperation remain critical.

In response, the Commission presented on 22 April 2026 the AccelerateEU communication1 with concrete measures to be taken immediately at Member States level in order to shield families and business alike, increase coordination and accelerate phase-out from fossil fuels, building on the lessons learnt with the 2022 crisis.

These measures must be targeted – protecting the most vulnerable, temporary and avoid worsening supply conditions, focusing on energy savings. They should accelerate the phasing out of fossil fuels by increasing the efficiency of the energy system and accelerating deployment of electrification and homegrown clean energy, including by better leveraging storage and demand flexibility for the benefit of consumers.

No EU-wide mechanism such as price ceiling is currently envisaged. Furthermore, the Commission will adopt a set of detailed recommendations to implement the Citizens Energy Package2, to help consumers bring down their bills.

These recommendations will aim at preventing consumer disconnections, prioritise consumer protection and switching to cheaper contracts, as well as expanding support for self-consumption and energy communities.

EU funds can play an important role in mitigating the impact of the current situation for example to support investments on energy efficiency; the setting up of an extraordinary fund to support Member States is not currently envisaged.
